sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) A person goes to France from India and buys a tour package from ABC India, who do all the travel document processing; ABC India is an outbound tour operator. (b) There are three types of travel agencies.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: there are two, retail and wholesale.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Thomas Cook was the first organised travel agent in the world. (b) A retail travel agency works as a retailer and sells package tours on behalf of a wholesaler.

Fill in the blanks. (a) Tourists expect the tour to be organised as per the ________ mentioned in the tour package (itinerary). (b) The difference between the retail price and the wholesale cost is the ________.
Fill in the blanks. (a) A ________ tour operator handles foreign tourists in the host country. (b) Thomas Cook created the ________ in 1873, the forerunner of the traveller's cheque.
True or False. (a) A wholesale travel agency earns by commission only. (b) An online travel agency works through a website connected to a global distribution system.
questions.answer: (a) False: it earns through volume discounts. (b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the meaning of a travel agency.
questions.answer: A travel agency is a business that arranges holidays and journeys by booking tickets, hotels and allied facilities. It acts as a retailer between the supplier and the tourist.

questions.q: What is meant by a mark-up price?
questions.answer: It is the price obtained by marking up the cost of a tour and selling it at a higher price. The difference between the retail price and the wholesale cost is the mark-up.

questions.q: Who is a ground operator? State two ground services.
questions.answer: A ground operator, also called a reception or destination management company, provides land arrangements at a destination. Services include local transport, guides and car rentals.

questions.q: Why are travel agencies and tour operators called intermediaries?
questions.answer: They bring together clients and the principal service providers. They strengthen the selling and buying process for both the customer and the hotels or airlines.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of a travel agency.
questions.answer: (i) It quotes fares and rates and makes reservations for air, rail and hotel. (ii) It arranges tickets, accommodation, travel insurance, foreign currency and documents. (iii) It accepts payments and acts as a single contact for the tourist.

questions.q: Distinguish between a retail travel agency and a wholesale travel agency with an example.
questions.answer: (i) A retail agency sells packages directly to tourists and earns commission; a wholesale agency buys in bulk and does not sell directly. (ii) A retail agency works on commission and mark-up; a wholesale agency earns through discounts on bulk reservations. (iii) For example, a local agency booking a Goa trip is a retailer while a firm that blocks hotel rooms and flight seats to make packages is a wholesaler.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of the outbound tour operators.
questions.answer: (i) They sell package tours to people of their own country for foreign destinations. (ii) They arrange travel documents and transportation to the starting point. (iii) They contract inbound or ground operators for accommodation, sightseeing and services abroad.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of a wholesale travel agency.
questions.answer: (i) It buys travel components in bulk from suppliers. (ii) It designs and assembles package tours. (iii) It sells packages through retail agents and provides consultancy, visa documents and currency exchange.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Who are inbound, outbound, domestic and ground operators? Explain with examples.
questions.answer: (i) Inbound operators handle foreign tourists in the host country; a French group handled by XYZ Travels in India. (ii) They are image builders and earn foreign exchange. (iii) Outbound operators send people of their country abroad, arranging documents; XYZ India sending a group to Singapore. (iv) Domestic operators work within the home country; Southern Travels' pilgrimage package for Chennai tourists to Amarnath. (v) Ground operators, also called reception operators or destination management companies, provide land arrangements. (vi) They provide transport, guides, events and accommodation where large companies have no local office.

questions.q: Differentiate between a tour operator, a retail travel agency and a wholesale travel agency, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) A tour operator is a wholesaler that creates its own packages; a retail agency sells on behalf of the wholesaler. (ii) A wholesale agency buys in bulk and does not sell to clients directly. (iii) A tour operator is based in mega cities; a retail agency can be anywhere. (iv) A tour operator is more inclined to ground handling; wholesale agencies are less so. (v) A retail agency works on commission; wholesalers earn on volume discounts. (vi) The size and multi-service capacity of a tour operator is high; of a wholesaler it is low.
